title: Open WebUI terminal proxy -- T1548 unsigned forwarded identity is spoofable via WebSocket session_id query injection
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-59224 (GHSA-j657-m4c4-24jq,
CVSS 8.0 HIGH -- corrected 2026-09-04 via live GHSA lookup, the rule's
original authoring understated this score), affecting Open WebUI's
terminal proxy.

The terminal proxy forwards the caller's identity to the upstream
terminal server as an unsigned claim, with no cryptographic binding
to the session that produced it. On the WebSocket path,
`ws_terminal()` in `backend/open_webui/routers/terminals.py`
interpolates the path parameter `session_id` directly into the
upstream URL before appending `?user_id=<caller>` -- and unlike its
HTTP sibling `proxy_terminal`, this path runs no `_sanitize_proxy_path`
or URL-encoding on `session_id`. An attacker-controlled `session_id`
containing an encoded `?`/`&` survives Open WebUI's single decode,
is re-decoded by the upstream, and injects an attacker-chosen
`user_id` ahead of the one Open WebUI appended -- and because query
parsing binds the first occurrence, the backend coordinator resolves
the spoofed user's terminal scope instead of the caller's own.

Detection logic flags a terminal WebSocket connect whose `session_id`
path segment contains a percent-encoded query delimiter (`%3F` or
`%26`) -- the exact injection primitive this advisory's unvalidated,
unencoded `session_id` concatenation makes possible.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact router functions and consolidating two
independent reports of the same root cause), fixed in Open WebUI
0.10.0+ (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's
original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note
corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
